belief: Family problems must be kept secret to protect the church.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that family problems must be kept secret to protect the church, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Being told not to “air dirty laundry” or hurt the church’s reputation. Pressure to protect a leader or respected family. Fear of shame, gossip, or being blamed. Families where abuse, addiction, or affairs were hidden. Teaching that honesty about problems is disloyal.
teaches: God loves truth and light. Scripture tells believers to expose deeds of darkness, not cover them. Whoever conceals sin will not prosper, but whoever confesses and turns from it finds mercy. God calls His people to defend the weak and rescue the oppressed. Private matters can be handled with discretion, but secrecy that protects harm is never God’s way. Protecting people, especially the vulnerable, matters more to God than protecting appearances.
self_statements: If I tell anyone, I’ll hurt the church.
We have to look like a good Christian family.
Talking about this would be gossip.
God wants me to protect our reputation.
It’s disloyal to ask for help.
If I speak up, I’ll be blamed.
errors: Valuing reputation above people’s safety and healing.
Staying silent because of fear of consequences.
Minimizing the damage that secrecy allows to continue.
questions: What does Ephesians 5:11 say to do with deeds of darkness?
Does keeping this secret protect people or protect harm?
Is anyone in danger, especially a child?
What is the difference between privacy and secrecy that hides wrongdoing?
What does God say about defending the weak and oppressed?
Who is a safe person I could tell?
What would healing look like for my family?
truth: Family problems do not have to be kept secret to protect the church. God loves truth and light, and He cares about the weak and hurting. I can handle private matters with discretion and still seek help. When someone is being harmed, speaking up is right. Healing begins when what is hidden is brought into the light.
hw_questions: What should I do with deeds of darkness?
Does secrecy protect people or harm?
Privacy or secrecy that hides wrong: which is this?
What does God say about the weak and oppressed?
Who is a safe person I could tell?
hw_truths: Protecting people matters more than protecting appearances.
God calls me to defend the weak.
Whoever confesses and turns from sin finds mercy.
Healing begins when hidden things come into the light.
log: Each day, write one true thing about my family’s situation and one step toward help or healing.
name_example: Then Sarah will know the truth, and the truth will set her free.
actions: Tell one safe person outside your family
to talk through your family situation.
If anyone is being abused or is in danger, contact the authorities.
In the U.S., the National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-7233 and the Childhelp hotline is 1-800-422-4453. In an emergency, call 911.
and write what God says about defending the vulnerable.
tracker: One step toward help or healing
prayer: Father, You love truth and light. Help me reject the lie that family problems must be kept secret to protect the church. Give me courage to seek help, wisdom to know whom to tell, and strength to protect anyone who is being hurt. Bring healing to my family. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
